# react-native-masonry-brick-list

> Pure-JS masonry / staggered grid ("brick list") for React Native and Expo. Items are placed on a fixed-column grid and can span several columns (`span`) and rows (`rowSpan`). No native modules. TypeScript types included.

Use it for tile mosaics, photo galleries with featured images, and dashboard-style grids where items are whole multiples of a cell. For a Pinterest-style waterfall, where every item is one column wide with its own height, use a column-based masonry list instead.

## Install

npm install react-native-masonry-brick-list

## Minimal example

```jsx
import BrickList from 'react-native-masonry-brick-list';

const data = [
  { id: '1', color: 'tomato' },
  { id: '2', color: 'gold', span: 2 },
  { id: '3', color: 'teal', rowSpan: 2 },
];

<BrickList
  data={data}
  columns={3}
  gap={8}
  renderItem={(item, index, cell) => <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: item.color }} />}
/>;
```

## Key facts

- Default export `BrickList`; named exports `BrickList`, `computeLayout`; types `BrickListItem`, `BrickListProps`, `BrickCell`, `PlacedCell`, `Layout`, `LayoutOptions`.
- `renderItem(item, index, cell)` takes positional arguments. It does NOT take FlatList's `({ item, index })` object. `cell` = `{ row, col, colSpan, rowSpan, width, height }` (width/height in points).
- Items: `id` (unique key), `span` (columns, default 1, clamped to `columns`), `rowSpan` (rows, default 1).
- Give the view returned by renderItem `flex: 1` so it fills its cell. Use `gap` for spacing, not margins.
- Props: `data`, `renderItem`, `columns` (3; `numColumns` is an alias), `rowHeight` (defaults to one column's width, so 1x1 cells are square), `gap` (0), `dense` (false), `keyExtractor`, `containerStyle`, `ListHeaderComponent`, `ListFooterComponent`, `ListEmptyComponent`, `onEndReached({ distanceFromEnd })`, `onEndReachedThreshold` (0.5).
- All other props go to the underlying ScrollView (`refreshControl`, `onScroll`, `contentContainerStyle`, ...). `ref` gives you the ScrollView (`ref.current.scrollTo({ y: 0 })`).
- Placement is row-major and never backfills, so visual order matches data order. `dense` backfills holes like CSS `grid-auto-flow: dense`.
- Not virtualized: every item mounts. Paginate long feeds with `onEndReached`.
- Vertical scrolling only. The grid mirrors automatically in RTL.
- `computeLayout(data, columns, { dense })` returns `{ cells, rows }` for custom renderers.
